slides.headline: Water-based or silicone? *One rule matters most.*
slides.lead: A two-minute guide to lube. Swipe.

slides.headline: More comfort. *More confidence.*
slides.body: Lube is quietly responsible for more of both than almost anything else. Reaching for it is nothing to hide.
slides.note: From intimova.ng: Water-based vs silicone lubricant.

slides.headline: The safe, *everyday default.*
slides.body: Safe with toys and latex condoms, rinses off with water and doesn’t stain. It can dry a little faster: a small top-up, or a drop of water, refreshes it.

slides.headline: Silkier, and it *lasts much longer.*
slides.body: Lovely skin to skin and with latex condoms, and water-resistant, so it holds up in the shower or bath.

slides.headline: Silicone toy? *Water-based lube.*
slides.body: Silicone lube can wear down the surface of a silicone toy over time. Keep it for skin to skin.

slides.headline: Sensitive skin? *Fragrance-free, glycerin-free.*
slides.body: Using latex condoms? Skip oil-based: it weakens latex. Not sure? Start water-based, the safe, versatile default.

slides.headline: Comfort isn’t extra. *It’s part of the point.*
slides.lead: Save this for later. Full guide: link in bio.

Water-based or silicone? One rule matters most. 💧

Water-based is the safe, everyday default: safe with toys and latex condoms, rinses off with water, doesn’t stain. Silicone is silkier, lasts much longer and holds up in the shower, lovely skin to skin.

The one rule: silicone toy, water-based lube. Silicone lube can wear down a silicone toy over time.

Sensitive skin? Look for fragrance-free, glycerin-free. Using latex condoms? Skip oil-based. Not sure? Start water-based.

Comfort isn’t extra. Reaching for lube is nothing to hide.
